1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the token hash against the session-bound resetTokenHash.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because it is session-bound and hashed.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after a password reset (session.recoveryGrantUntil is cleared, and authenticated is set).

4.why: The website enforces HTTPS with TLS (certs/cert.pem and certs/key.pem are required).

5.why: Reset codes are hashed using SHA-256, and user data is not stored in plaintext (Argon2id for passwords).

6.why: Email messages do not expose private user data (generic response regardless of account existence).

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is validated (safeEmail, strongPassword) and sanitized (JSON parsing, allow-list checks).

8.why: Redirect links are not used; only local hash-based navigation is allowed (no outgoing URLs).

9.why: Email templates are not dynamically generated from user input; simulated logs use textContent.

10.why: Error pages and logs do not expose private information or tokens (generic messages).

11.why: Passwords and secret codes are stored securely (Argon2id hashing, no plaintext in code).

12.why: No default credentials are present; sessions are randomly generated.

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (generic response).

15.why: The password reset code is random (randomValue(32)), complex, and user-specific (session-bound).
